---
title: "Automated Planning Engine (PDDL)"
subtitle: "Heuristic search planning with aggressive state-space reduction"
---

A PDDL based planning engine for complex multi-agent logistics and scheduling problems, solved with the Fast Downward planning system. The focus is on taming combinatorial explosions through heuristic search and strict state-space reduction. Built for the Intelligent Systems Techniques course (Técnicas de los Sistemas Inteligentes, 2025-26) of the Computer Science and Mathematics double degree at the University of Granada.

[View source on GitHub](https://github.com/laurasalop03/pddl-automated-planning-engine){.btn .btn-outline-secondary}

## Algorithmic highlights

- **Symmetry breaking**: enforced lexicographical ordering between interchangeable agents to cut exponential branching in multi-agent states.
- **Dimensionality reduction**: grouped individual agents into a single macro-entity for traversal actions, reducing action parameters from 7 to 2. This cut $A^*$ search time from nearly 12 minutes (698 seconds) to under 1 minute on complex states.
- **Axiom and quantifier optimization**: redesigned the domain to avoid existential quantifiers in goal states, triggering direct boolean predicates instead. This prevented derived axioms and kept the model compatible with optimal heuristics such as `seq-opt-lmcut`.
- **Anytime cost optimization**: custom metric functions for non-uniform traversal weights, using `seq-sat-lama-2011` to find valid plans quickly and then iteratively minimize total cost.

## Why it is relevant to quant work

This is optimization under combinatorial explosion, and the headline result (a roughly 12x speedup, from 698 seconds to under a minute, by reformulating the model) is exactly the kind of problem reformulation that separates a tractable quant model from an intractable one. Choosing the right heuristic and encoding is often worth more than raw compute.

## Tech

PDDL, Fast Downward, $A^*$ search, LM-cut heuristics, LAMA-2011.
